image_description: A close-up, macro photograph of a bright yellow coral fungus (likely Ramaria or Clavulinopsis species) growing from dark, mossy soil. The fungus features multiple upright, cylindrical branches that fork near the tips, resembling marine coral. The background is softly blurred (bokeh), showing hints of green leaves and brown earth.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific taxonomic classification and rule out look-alike structures or hallucinated species features.
To verify that individual branches are distinct entities and do not merge or melt into each other or the background, a common AI artifact in complex branching structures.
To assess texture realism, lighting consistency, and detect subtle noise or blur artifacts typical of generative models.
To ensure the depth of field (bokeh) is physically consistent with a macro lens and that the fungus sits correctly in the 3D space of the forest floor.

focus_areas: Tip definition (no blurring or extra limbs)
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the tips of the branches. AI generators often struggle with terminating thin structures cleanly, resulting in blunt ends, merging tips, or 'ghost' extensions. Also, verify the boundary between the yellow fungus and the dark soil; look for haloing or color bleeding which indicates poor segmentation during generation.
